summary: Docs-only commit; no test file is staged, so nothing was weakened (verified: git status --short shows only docs + baselines). Reviewed as test guidance: does the prose make an M4.10c/M4.10d author write tests that fail when the production code is wrong. Verified against the tree: BatchingSequencerTest:259-261 does commitAll(from("pod0",0), from("pod1",0)) with hasSize(2) as its only delta assertion; BatchedCommitDeltaTest:52 asserts whole-record equality on a three-segment fixture; GoldenChainEntryTest javadoc really says 'Do NOT regenerate these to make the test pass'; chain-delta-batched-v1.bin really holds bins/a.seg with no pod; CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest:117 really is bytes[7]=1; CheckpointTest:169 really is isLessThan(64*1024) with a ~38 KiB 1,600-stream body; CheckpointWriter:126-129's Math::max comment really argues for the behaviour M4.10d must not have; DefaultIngest:349 really increments flushSeq inside the throwing call; IngestCommitPathTest's Recording seam really can hold the two-instance/two-flush incarnation fixture; zero production 'new BatchingSequencer' (25, all tests), so the byte-equivalence claim holds. Three minors, all prose-level, none of which stops M4.10c being built correctly by an author who reads the whole section.

findings.title: The ADR still carries the fixture instruction backlog-notes.md now falsifies, and the ADR is the normative half
findings.failure_scenario: The clause 'on a fixture whose triple varies in at least one field per segment' is satisfied by varying podId ALONE -- which is exactly the condition under which the mutation named two sentences later survives. The M4.10c row headline says 'per ADR-0036', and wire-format-change sends a session to the ADR, so an author can reasonably build from the ADR alone: a three-segment fixture with three distinct podIds and one shared incarnation/flushSeq, asserting the per-segment triple after round-trip and after commitAll. That suite is green over the PARTIAL hoist. backlog-notes.md:263 now states the opposite ('every fixture already varies by podId, so "vary one field per segment" is satisfied today and buys nothing'), so the tree carries a corrected claim and its uncorrected duplicate -- the shape already filed twice as M4.42 and M4.45, and named in the M4.10a baselines entry as 'deleting the section missed its duplicate'. Answering the question put to this round: the notes carrying it is NOT enough, because the falsified sentence is still standing in the accepted decision record.
findings.surviving_mutation: PARTIAL hoist of the encoder: write podId per SegmentCommit but write incarnationId and flushSeq ONCE per delta, copying them onto every segment on decode. BatchedCommitDeltaTest's decoded.isEqualTo(original) still passes because the fixture's segments share incarnation and flushSeq; BatchingSequencerTest's commitAll fixture is from("pod0",0)/from("pod1",0), identical flushSeq by construction, so a per-segment triple assertion there passes too. Production drops every pod but one on M5's first forwarded multi-pod batch -- the exact harm the placement clause exists to prevent.
findings.suggested_fix: DELETE the clause ', on a fixture whose triple varies in at least one field per segment' (a deletion, not a rewording -- it has now been wrong for three rounds, and a deletion cannot add a fourth claim). The following sentence already names the partial hoist, and backlog-notes.md:260-268 carries the sharper statement.

findings.title: 'ELEVEN JAVA SITES' is one short of the list it introduces, and the missing one is the load-bearing site
findings.failure_scenario: git grep -n 'podId, flushSeq' -- '*.java' returns 11 lines across 8 files (measured). The sentence says ELEVEN sites and that the grep 'finds all but one', naming Sequencer.java:48-50 as the unmatched one -- so the total is 11 + 1 = 12, and the enumerated list that follows has exactly 12 entries (Sequencer 35/46/88/48-50, CommitRequest 19, FakeSequencer 27/29, FakeSequencerTest 178, Checkpoint 32, IngestCommitPathTest 81, CommitProtocolSimulation 58, CommitProtocolSimulationFlushSeqTest 23). An M4.10c session that uses the numeral as its completion check greps, counts 11, matches 'ELEVEN', and stops -- leaving standing precisely the site the sentence exists to rescue, the one the next paragraph says is 'Falsified by ADR-0036 and load-bearing' and which tells an M4.10d session to key dedup on the bare pair while every single-incarnation M4 fixture stays green and a restarted pod is SUPPRESSED. Off by one in the direction that costs the whole sentence its purpose.
findings.surviving_mutation: Not a code mutation: the numeral itself is the check that survives being wrong. Grep returns 11, the prose says 11, the sweep reports done, and Sequencer.java:48-50 ('carried from this first commit precisely so M4.10 can make the retry safe without changing the record shape') ships contradicting the accepted ADR.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop the numeral rather than correct it a third time -- 'THE SITES BELOW, ACROSS EIGHT FILES, ARE THIS ROW'S' -- since the enumerated list is the authority and a count is what keeps going stale.

findings.title: The DO-NOT-REGENERATE clause is right and conflicts with nothing, but it leaves the legacy golden's re-encode assertion unprotected
findings.failure_scenario: Verified: GoldenChainEntryTest's javadoc does say 'Do NOT regenerate these to make the test pass', chain-delta-batched-v1.bin is the only v1-KINDED delta golden, it holds bins/a.seg with no pod, and the clause does not conflict with the new-golden requirement -- the ADR (:133) and that test's own javadoc ('another version and another golden file') both say the discriminating golden is a NEW file. The gap is the rest of that test. aBatchedDeltaFromAnEarlierBuildStillParses also asserts at GoldenChainEntryTest:75 via containsExactly(new SegmentCommit(key, runs)) -- the two-arg constructor -- and at :81-84 that delta.encode() is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the golden. Adding three fields to SegmentCommit breaks both. The clause forbids the regeneration route but says nothing about the re-encode assertion, so the cheapest green is to delete or loosen it, which check-test-integrity.sh only catches if it recognises the loosening.
findings.surviving_mutation: An encoder that ALWAYS emits the triple-carrying shape. The legacy golden still DECODES, so the do-not-regenerate clause is honoured and aBatchedDeltaFromAnEarlierBuildStillParses is green once the :81-84 byte-identity assertion is dropped -- while every delta in every bucket churns to a new shape on rewrite, which is the property aSingleSegmentDeltaIsStillWrittenAsV0SoNoBucketChurns and the ADR's own M3.0 citation exist to hold.
findings.suggested_fix: One clause beside the existing one: the legacy golden's byte-identical re-encode assertion must SURVIVE, so canonical encoding stays legacy-preserving -- a delta no segment of which carries a triple re-encodes to the v1 kinded bytes it arrived as.

criteria_coverage: M4.10b's deliverable is the ADR itself, so 'would this test fail if the production code were wrong' applies to the guidance rather than to code. Each of the six properties the row states is answered in ADR-0036 with a named mutation an M4.10c/d author must kill: replay ANSWERED not merely detected (the pointer, plus the refuse-rather-than-return-another-flush's-offsets bound); no object grows with history (value beside flushSeq, not a qualifier on the pod id; the 32-bytes-per-pod arithmetic checked against CheckpointTest:169's real 64 KiB bound and real ~38 KiB body); no commit-path request scales with pods; survives a truncating checkpoint (the ChainReplay.applyChain argument, verified against the Hop javadoc's 'never GET at all'); which formats change (both, with both delta encodings named); and the pre-change checkpoint (the enumerated {0,1} requirement, with the mutation 'version <= VERSION' named AND the vacuity of CheckpointDecodeRefusalTest:117's bytes[7]=1 called out -- that is the strongest item in the ADR and is exactly this role's kind of finding, written by the author). The minting-site clause is the one that would otherwise have shipped a no-op: it names the per-FLUSH mutation, states that every sequencer-seam suite stays green under it, and names the only fixture that can see it, with both directions (two instances sharing a podShortId must record DIFFERENT incarnations, one instance's two flushes the SAME one) -- which also kills a podShortId-derived deterministic incarnation. No acceptance criterion of this row is left without a mutation an author must kill.
tier_and_standards: No tier question: no test is staged. No testing.md rule is engaged by the diff. The guidance keeps M4.10c's discriminating work in T0 (format round-trip, golden, the ingest recording seam) rather than reaching for a socket or a clock, and the one clock-shaped claim in the ADR (the 200/200 frozen-clock measurement, and the explicit refusal to call the 175/200 systemUTC number a production rate) is disclosed as a fixture artifact rather than quoted as a rate.
